title: Viewport on systems with displays with scaled resolutions has sizing issues on Linux. Both Wayland and X11.
body: ### Tested versions v4.5.beta5.official Tested on all 3 renderers. ### System information Godot v4.5.beta5 - Fedora Linux 42 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - integrated Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (TGL GT2) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-11370H @ 3.30GHz (8 threads) - 62.52 GiB memory ### Issue description Both on **X11** and **Wayland** the viewport has sizing issues, if the system has displays with scaling set in system settings. This has been tested on a laptop with 3 displays: - Screen 01: resolution 2880x1800 , scaling 175% - Screen 02: resolution 3840x2160 , scaling 150% - Screen 03: resolution 1920x1080 , scaling 100% If I understand the results correctly some issues will still be present also if the system has just one display, as long as the resolution scale set to anything but 100%. However, this is most clear if there are more than 1 display. The issue on Wayland is slightly different from issue on X11, but they have similarities. In both cases `DisplayServer.window_get_size()` returns invalid values for everything that is not the first display (it doesn't have to be the "main" display, just the first connected/recognised). It would seem that Godot takes the scale of the first found display and uses it for all scaling moving forward, regardless of the display the window is on. On **Wayland** the general behaviour is that the window size is correct, but all the sizes of 2D elements within the viewport scale incorrectly. On **X11** the general behaviour is that the window sizes are incorrect, but the scale of 2D elements vs. the viewport is correct. **In all sreenshots the window is set to be 1280x720 and the Godot icon to 128x128.** It is a 3D scene with a sphere in the centre with 2D texture rect on a panel as the UI overlay. ### WAYLAND Main Screen. Native Resolution 2880 x 1800. Scaling 1.75. Displayed viewport: 2240x1260 (after scaling: 1280 x 720) - **correct** Displayed Godot icon: 128 x 128 (after scaling: 73 x 73) - **incorrect** `DisplayServer.window_get_size()` returns 2880 x 1800 - **correct** `get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size` returns 2240 x 1260 - **this is the displayed viewport size, but we should be getting the scaled value** Second Screen. Native Resolution 1920 x 1080. Scaling 1.0. Displayed viewport: 1280 x 720 - **correct** Displayed Godot icon: 128 x 128 - **correct** `DisplayServer.window_get_size()` returns 2880 x 1800 - **incorrect** `get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size` returns 1280 x 720 - **correct** ### X11 Main Screen. Native Resolution 2880 x 1800. Scaling 1.75. Displayed viewport: 1280x720 (after scaling: 732 x 411) - **incorrect** Displayed Godot icon: 128 x 128 (after scaling: 73 x 73) - **scales correctly to viewport, but incorrect in general** `DisplayServer.window_get_size()` returns 2880 x 1800 - **correct** `get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size` returns 1280 x 720 - **this should be the viewport size, but isn't** Second Screen. Native Resolution 1920 x 1080. Scaling 1.0. Displayed viewport: 732 x 411 - **incorrect** Displayed Godot icon: 73 x 73 - **scales correctly to viewport, but incorrect in general** `DisplayServer.window_get_size()` returns 3360 x 1890 - **incorrect** `get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size` returns 1280 x 720 - **this should be the viewport size, but isn't** ### Steps to reproduce 1. Set resolution scaling in your system settings. 2. Create a new project with a 3D scene and put any 2D element in the viewport. 3. Run the project. 4. X11: the window size will be incorrect. Wayland: the 2D element size will be incorrect ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [resolution_bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21898561/resolution_bug.zip)
